labels.text: Create a project in the account.
Created '{}' in your account ({}).

S23.01.note: The printed line shows the real name and id; the label is the code's format string.
steps: In a terminal, type: agi projects create "QA Test Project" (add --description "Test text" if you want a description).
Look for the line: Created 'QA Test Project' in your account (<id>).
Type: agi projects list.
Look for a row with the id and the name QA Test Project in the list.
S23.01.where: agi projects create <name>, then agi projects list

labels.text: Optional description.
Rename a project or change its description or instructions.

steps: Type: agi projects create "QA Described" --description "First description".
Type: agi projects show "QA Described" and look for the line "First description" under the project name.
Type: agi projects edit "QA Described" --description "Changed description".
Type: agi projects show "QA Described" and check that the description now reads "Changed description".
S23.02.where: agi projects create <name> --description <text>, then agi projects edit <project> --description <text>, then agi projects show <project>

labels.text: Show one project: description, instructions, knowledge files and conversation count.
Knowledge files

S23.05.needs: a signed-in account and a project
S23.05.note: The screen has no separate chats or files heading; it shows a Conversations count, Instructions and Knowledge files lines.
steps: Type: agi projects show "QA Described" (use a project id or name from agi projects list).
Look for the id and name on the first line, then the description line indented under it.
Look for "Conversations:" with a number, then "Instructions:" (or "Instructions: none").
Look for "Knowledge files: none" or a "Knowledge files (<n>):" list, and compare with Expected.

labels.text: Link this directory to an account project by id or name.
Show only the account conversations filed under this project (id or name).
Resume one with `agi resume --cloud <id>`.

S23.06.needs: a signed-in account and a folder to link
S23.06.note: New chats are filed under a project only when started from a folder linked to it; no CLI flag starts a chat directly in a project.
steps: Go to a folder in Terminal and type: agi projects link "QA Described".
Start agi in the same folder, send one message, and exit.
Type: agi history --project "QA Described" and look for the heading "Conversations in QA Described:" with your chat listed.
Type: agi resume --cloud <id> using the id shown in that list, and check the chat opens.
S23.06.where: agi projects link <project>, then agi in that folder, then agi history --project <project>, then agi resume --cloud <id>

labels.text: Rename a project or change its description or instructions.
their conversations are filed under it.

S23.09.needs: a signed-in account and a folder to link
S23.09.note: The code applies project instructions only to chats started from the folder linked to the project, not to every chat in the project as Expected says.
steps: In a folder, type: agi projects link "QA Described".
Type: agi projects edit "QA Described" --instructions "Always answer in one short sentence."
Type: agi projects show "QA Described" and check the Instructions text is shown.
Start agi in that same folder, ask a question, and compare the answer with the instruction.
S23.09.where: agi projects link <project>, then agi projects edit <project> --instructions <text>, then agi in that folder

labels.text: Keep it with the account project this directory is linked to
Remembered in your account, on every client.

S23.11.needs: a signed-in account and a folder linked to a project
S23.11.note: Project memory and account-wide memory are both added here, but no per-project switch to stop a project drawing on account-wide memory was found; account memory is turned on or off for the whole account with agi memory on or off.
steps: In a folder linked to a project (agi projects link), type: agi memory add "Prefer short answers" --project.
Look for the line that says the memory was remembered in this project's memory.
Type: agi memory list and look for the new memory with the tag ", this project".
Type: agi memory add "Use metric units" (no --project), then agi memory list, and check it has no project tag.
S23.11.where: agi memory add <text> --project (in a linked folder), then agi memory list

labels.text: Only the artifacts of this project id.
Print an artifact's content, or write it to a file.
List the account's artifacts, newest first.

S23.12.needs: a signed-in account and an artifact made in a project chat
S23.12.note: The --project option takes a project id, not a name.
steps: Type: agi projects list and copy the id of the project.
Type: agi artifacts list --project <project id> and look for artifacts from that project's chats.
Type: agi artifacts show <artifact id> and check the content prints.
Type: agi artifacts open <artifact id> and check it opens the published page or the chat it came from.
S23.12.where: agi artifacts list --project <project id>, then agi artifacts show <id> or agi artifacts open <id>

S23.13.note: The cited apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2876 lists conversations filed under a project ('Conversations in'), not coding sessions; no separate CLI listing of project coding sessions was found.

S23.17.note: The CLI project record has no default tools or Skills field (apps/cli/src/cloud/projects.rs); the cited skills.rs code covers user and folder disabled skills, not account project defaults. The web projects tests mention chatDefaults, but the web app is not this CLI.

labels.text: Link this directory to an account project by id or name.
Recent project folders

S23.18.needs: a signed-in account and a folder on this Mac
steps: Go to a folder on this Mac in Terminal.
Type: agi projects link "QA Described" and check the line that says the folder is linked to the account project 'QA Described'.
Type: agi projects recent and look for this folder in the list of recent project folders.
Start agi in this folder and check that the project's instructions and knowledge are used (compare with Expected).
S23.18.where: agi projects link <project>, then agi projects recent

labels.text: Archive a project so it leaves the active list without being deleted.
Bring an archived project back instead.

S23.30.needs: a signed-in account and a project
S23.30.note: The CLI list keeps archived projects and marks them [archived] rather than removing them from the list.
steps: Type: agi projects archive "QA Described" and look for the line Archived 'QA Described' (<id>) in your account.
Type: agi projects list and look for the tag [archived] on that project.
Type: agi projects show "QA Described" and check its description and conversation count are still there.
Type: agi projects archive "QA Described" --undo, look for the Unarchived line, and check the tag is gone from agi projects list.
S23.30.where: agi projects archive <project>, then agi projects archive <project> --undo

labels.text: Delete a project from the account by id or name.
Delete project '

S23.32.needs: a signed-in account and a throwaway project
S23.32.note: The prompt warns that knowledge files are deleted and conversations stay unfiled; no owner-only check was seen in the CLI code, so the server decides.
steps: Type: agi projects delete "QA Test Project" (use a throwaway project).
At the prompt that starts Delete project 'QA Test Project'?, type n and check the line Left the project in place.
Type the command again and answer y.
Look for Deleted project 'QA Test Project' (<id>) from your account., then type agi projects list and check the project is gone.

labels.text: /thread <instruction> starts a parallel thread with a copy of this conversation.
/gather brings the finished ones back here.

S23.36.needs: a signed-in account and a conversation that is being saved
S23.36.note: In a conversation that is not being saved, /thread says it has no threads; that is the 'where offered' limit.
steps: Start agi, sign in, and open a conversation that is being saved.
Type: /thread Summarise the last answer in three bullets. Check the message says a thread started on a copy of this conversation.
Type: /threads and check the thread shows a state such as running or finished.
When a thread has finished, type: /gather and check its result is brought back into this conversation.
